confirmed.title: Saving silently stops working after roughly 40 turns: a 10-turn chunk document outgrows the 256 KiB db limit
confirmed.summary: Every stored turn embeds stateBefore, stateAfter, memBefore (a full copy of the memory incl. up to 600 events), pendingBefore and all regenerated alts; persist() writes 10 turns per document, so a chunk grows past 262,144 bytes and set() rejects invalid_argument. Transformation tracks keep their full drawn step texts in state.tf.tracks and every turn clones the whole state twice, which brings the failure forward to turn ~20 (or ~10 with six tracks).
confirmed.scenario: A player reaches turn ~40 in one adventure (turn ~20 in Sundered once three species tracks are alive, turn ~10 with six tracks); every later turn fails to save; closing the tab or opening on another device loses all progress after the last good save; dirty flag stays set so the page also keeps offering conflicts. The only user-visible signal is the small Summary-panel note.
confirmed.evidence: Lead probe (probe2.js, strict mock, 380-word narratives, 3 events/beats per turn): chunks 126K, 196K, 243K KiB at turns 10/20/30; turn 39 -> save failed: invalid_argument, violation doc-too-large adventures/<id>/turns/0003 is 266688 bytes (cap 262144). probe_st_24 (tracks): turn 20 save failed, chunks 202K/256K, doc-too-large turns/0001 294873 bytes; probe_st_25 (6 species): turn 10 save failed, turns/0000 275768 bytes. Code: tracks.push({... steps: drawSteps(content.steps) ...}) 1016; stateBefore/stateAfter: clone(state) 1544.
confirmed.repro: node C:/Users/marcu/AppData/Local/Temp/wl-harness/probe2.js (prints FIRST FAILURE turn 39); probes/probe_st_24.js and probes/probe_st_25.js
confirmed.fix: Store only what is needed per turn (drop memBefore/stateBefore or store diffs/hashes), keep track step texts out of per-turn snapshots (store indexes and look text up from world data), size chunks by bytes not by count of 10, and surface a persistent save-failed banner.

confirmed.title: Import writes only the last chunk of turns to the store, so an imported adventure loses its earlier turns on reload
confirmed.summary: importFile() builds a new adventure with all imported turns, then calls persist(), which writes the adventure doc and only the final 10-turn chunk. persistAll() (which writes every chunk) is not used.
confirmed.scenario: Player exports a 25-turn save, imports it (e.g. on another device or after deleting the original); the page looks right until reload/sync, then turns 1-10 are gone while turnCount still says 19.
confirmed.evidence: Lead probe (probe3.js): original adventure has chunk docs 0000,0001; imported copy has turnCount 19 but only chunk 0001 in the store.
confirmed.fix: Call persistAll(adv.id) after import (and verify with a read-back).

votes.reasoning: importFile (index.html:1857-1869) builds adv with all p.turns, then calls only persist() at 1867; persist (1753-1768) writes the adventure doc plus just the final chunk (chunkIdx = floor((n-1)/CHUNK), CHUNK=10 at 499). persistAll (1769-1775) is called only from overwriteStore (1745) and the Save-a-copy handler (1824), never from import. loadAdventure (1781-1784) rebuilds turns solely from the chunk docs, so any earlier chunk absent from the store is gone on reload, and nothing in the normal turn path rewrites earlier chunks. My own probe reproduced it on a shared store with a fresh second page: 14 turns exported, the imported copy has only chunk 0001 (turns 11-14) while turnCount stays 14, and the reloaded page shows Turn 0 and Turns 11-14, with turns 1-10 missing. Scope notes: saves of 10 or fewer turns are unaffected, and the export file and the original adventure still hold the data (so it is silent truncation of the imported copy, not loss of the only copy unless the original was deleted). The finding's scenario numbers (25 turns, turnCount 19) do not match the probe runs (15 and 14 turns), but this does not change the conclusion. A persistAll fix is also subject to K1's 256 KiB chunk cap on long saves.
votes.corrected_summary: Confirmed as stated. Narrow scope: it applies to imports of saves with more than 10 turns (CHUNK=10), and the original and the export file still hold the full history.

Account for the K1 256 KiB per-chunk cap, since long imported saves would otherwise fail in persistAll and the import should surface that error.

confirmed.title: An in-flight turn (or roommate intro) is committed into whichever adventure is loaded when the reply arrives
confirmed.summary: takeTurn, commitReply and writeRoommateIntro keep using the global adv/W after their awaits, but Continue, New adventure/Begin, Import, Delete-current and the boot load replace adv without checking busy (only #reloadAdv and #overwriteAdv check it, lines 2483-2484; setBusyUI disables only send/regen/regenWith/undo). The reply is applied to and persisted into the wrong adventure (processed under the other world's rules); a failed or stopped turn instead assigns its stateBefore to the other adventure (1608).
confirmed.scenario: Start a turn (30-120 s on the complex tier), open Adventures and press Continue on another save, or Import, or New adventure > Begin. When the reply lands it is pushed into the other adventure, its clock/state advance and it is saved there; the original never receives the turn, and a later Undo writes the foreign state into it. A roommate intro still being written after Begin goes to the new adventure with the OLD roommate's text. The same race exists at boot: a turn sent before db resolves lands in the freshly loaded save.
confirmed.evidence: probe_p5_2: A turns in store ['1:A first action','2:B SLOW action'], B keeps only turn 1. probe_c1_switch/_switch2: after the slow turn current adv B has A's action, store B turns/0000 holds it; new-adventure variant B clock 09:10 -> 09:25. probe_cr_3: new adventure B has 'SLOW ACTION FROM ADVENTURE A', turnCount 1; probe_cr_15: B gets A's roommate intro. probe_rend_4/_20, probe_p1_2 (sundered/halloway cross-world), probe_rt_3, probe_ps_6/_7 (S5-S7, H9a/b boot race), probe_ui_24/_35 all show the wrong-adventure commit; probe_p5_17: Undo writes Halloway state into the Sundered adventure.
confirmed.repro: probes/probe_p5_2.js, probe_c1_switch.js, probe_cr_3.js, probe_cr_15.js, probe_rend_4.js, probe_rend_20.js, probe_p1_2.js, probe_rt_3.js, probe_ps_6.js, probe_ps_7.js, probe_ui_24.js, probe_ui_35.js
confirmed.fix: Refuse (or disable the buttons for) Continue/New/Import/Delete/Begin while busy or while boot loading runs, and capture const mine = adv at the start of takeTurn/writeRoommateIntro and discard the commit and persist (and the rollback) if adv !== mine after any await.

confirmed.title: Prompt-size guard cannot shrink the largest sections and never re-checks its last step; long Sundered games dead-end with prompt_too_large
confirmed.summary: The guard only trims timeline events, older beats and the verbatim window, then sends the last candidate without measuring it. Lore (up to ~10K), characters (~8.5K), gm_only (~5K), transformation (~7K), facts (up to 60, ~10 KB) and summary are never reduced, and the memory fold runs only after a successful turn. Sundered's base prompt is already ~52 KB.
confirmed.scenario: Standard Sundered game with 3 facts of ~30 words per turn: the guard engages at turn 7 and turn 18 fails with 'Prompt too large ... lower the verbatim window', although the window is already forced to 1 and Settings offers only 2-4. Every retry fails; only emptying the summary or Undo gets out. Sundered with several kinds at influence >= 15 hits 66,073 bytes after the last guard step.

confirmed.title: 'Save a copy' makes the copy the most recent save and mutates the live adv.title across awaits, so a racing save renames the original
confirmed.summary: The copy's updatedAt is newer than the adventure being played, and boot opens the most recently saved adventure; the copy handler also swaps the live adv.title across the awaits of persistAll(newId), so a double-click on OK or any persist() (a turn finishing, a settings change) serialises the temporary title and renames the original.
confirmed.scenario: A player saves a backup copy before a risky choice and closes the tab; on reopen (or another device) the page loads the copy and play continues there with nothing in the main view showing the title. With a racing save, or a double-click on OK, both docs (or two copies) end up titled '... (copy)'.

(copy)' after next save.
confirmed.fix: Pass the title into persistAll instead of mutating adv.title, give the copy an updatedAt at or below the source's so the source stays the latest save, and disable OK while the copy is being written.

A second click therefore captures oldTitle = t and permanently restores the copy title (probe_rend_11 reproduced 2 copies plus the original renamed). confirmed.title: Export filename .slice(0, 80) cuts off '.json', so long titles always fail with rejected_extension and fall into a JSON dump
confirmed.summary: (W.id + '-' + slug + '.json').slice(0, 80) removes the extension whenever the slug exceeds about 65 characters, which downloads.save rejects with rejected_extension; the catch then dumps the whole JSON into #exportFallback for any non-'declined' error (including rate_limited from a double click) with the generic 'download unavailable' note, and the pre is never hidden again. confirmed.title: Memory fold and length fit accept any utility-model reply (refusal, truncated text, preamble, 3,000 words)
confirmed.summary: foldBeats replaces the summary with whatever text comes back, then permanently discards the 18 beats and 20 facts it was meant to merge. fitLength results are checked only for more than 50 words, and res.truncated is never read.
confirmed.scenario: A quick-tier refusal, truncated or one-word reply becomes the whole long-term summary and the folded beats are gone from memory and later prompts; a truncated fit, one with a 'Here's the rewritten passage:' preamble, or one longer than the input becomes the committed narrative.

Observed: summary now "I'm sorry, but I can't help with that request.", beats 43 -> 25; also summary 'Done.'; fit note 'length fitted 900 -> 3000 words'; truncated fit accepted.
confirmed.fix: Reject fold or fit results that are truncated, outside a sane length window (summary roughly 40-400 words, fit within the band) or refusal-shaped, and keep the old summary and narrative.

I reran probe_eng_11.js and got the reported output: refusal text, 'Done.', a truncated fragment and a 16,333-char summary were all committed with beats 43 -> 25, and the fit cases committed a preamble, a truncated 200-word text and a 3000-word text ('length fitted 900 -> 3000 words'). The claim is overstated in four ways. (1) It is not permanent: the fold turn's `memBefore` holds the old summary and beats, so Undo or Regenerate on that turn restores them (1680, 1688); per-turn `beats` stay in the turn log and still feed the `earlier_turns` block (1325); and the summary textarea is visible and editable (2385, 2417). (2) A real API refusal rejects with `refused` per sample.d.ts:595, which lands in the catch at 1549 and keeps the old summary, so only a soft in-text refusal gets through. (3) A short refusal can never be accepted as a fit, because of the >50-word gate, and the 'Done.' and 3000-word cases need unrealistic model output. (4) The realistic triggers are `truncated: true` (documented in sample.d.ts:481 as possible but usually false), a preamble line on fit, or a rambling over-length summary. Those are rare, but the failure is silent and compounds, because the bad summary is fed into later folds. Medium severity is defensible.

confirmed.title: Async handlers lack in-flight guards: double-click Undo removes two turns, double-click Take turn / Ctrl+Enter leaves a stale red banner, double OK / Begin re-enter
confirmed.summary: onUndo, onRegenerate and onSend check busy before awaiting syncFromStore(), and syncFromStore() returns false (carry on) when re-entered while syncing, so a second click passes the guard while the first is awaiting the db read. Ctrl+Enter ignores the disabled Take turn button; the inline OK and Begin buttons are re-enterable too.
confirmed.scenario: With a realistic db round trip, a double-click on Undo pops two turns (3 -> 1, stored turnCount 1) and issues overlapping writes; with one turn left the second click throws a TypeError. A double-click on Take turn, or Ctrl+Enter during a turn, leaves a red 'A turn is already running.' after the turn succeeds; without sample it replaces the banner holding the Retry button. A double-click on Begin is read as 'Begin now' and aborts all six invention calls after 0.1 s.
confirmed.evidence: probe_eng_7 (150 ms db, clicks 40 ms apart): turns 4 -> 2, store turnCount 2, overlapping-writes violations; Take turn: final status 'A turn is already running.' [bad]; probe_ui_30 (120 ms): 'before turns 3 -> after double-click Undo turns 1', with one turn TypeError reading 'stateBefore' at onUndo; probe_rend_9/9b: Ctrl+Enter -> Retry button gone / red banner persists; probe_rend_7: double Begin 'stopped after 0.1 s; 0 of 5 kept' x6; probe_rend_12: 6 unhandled {code:'aborted'}; probe_cr_2 pt3: 2nd Begin click made 0 invention calls.

confirmed.fix: Set a synchronous in-flight flag at the top of onUndo/onRegenerate/onSend/OK/Begin before any await and clear it in finally; gate Ctrl+Enter on busy and sample; make a re-entered syncFromStore make the caller bail rather than proceed; ignore a Begin re-click for ~1 s.

confirmed.summary: openCreate() calls randomAll(), which calls inventPlayerFields(), so every dialog open (including the automatic first-run open at boot) and every 'Randomise everything' makes a consent-triggering sample call with a random-seeded, never-stable prompt. confirmed.title: Clicking the 'Two things you are good at' label re-rolls the player's strengths
confirmed.summary: The Random button sits inside the field's <label> with no for attribute, so the label's control is that button and any click or tap on the caption (or the empty rest of its full-width row) fires Random; the checkbox group also has no group name.
confirmed.scenario: A player carefully picks two strengths and a weakness, then taps the caption: the choices change at random without any prompt and focus jumps to Random.
confirmed.evidence: <label>Two things you are good at <button data-rand="traits">Random</button></label>; Chromium label.control is the BUTTON; label.click() changed the checked set 'charm,vigour' -> 'nerve,charm' (6 clicks each changed it); a real mouse click changed 'charm,vigour | weak=nerve' to 'charm,empathy | wits'; the label is 843px wide.
confirmed.repro: Browser pane at http://127.0.0.1:4173/ (New adventure dialog; label.control, label.click())
confirmed.fix: Move the Random button out of the <label> and make the checks container a fieldset/legend or role=group with aria-labelledby.

votes.reasoning: index.html:345 has `<label>` with no `for` that contains the `data-rand="traits"` button. `.field` is display:grid (index.html:141), so the label is blockified to the full row width, and the button is its only labelable descendant, so label.control is the button. The only click handler is `b.onclick` at index.html:2499, which calls randomField('traits') (index.html:2114-2119), unchecks all boxes, then re-picks two strengths and a weakness. Nothing guards against a click forwarded from the label, and `.checks` (index.html:344-345) has no role=group or aria-labelledby. Two real mouse clicks in the browser both re-rolled the choices. The finding's line cite "2028" is wrong (the handler is at 2499 and the logic at 2107-2119), and the impact is recoverable by re-picking, so medium is the upper end.

confirmed.title: Halloway reach-salt code flag is never explained to the model, and the fever-break note misfires for salt fevers
confirmed.summary: salt_taken_this_turn appears in the model prompt only as a key inside <state>; no rule or <progression> text says to set it, and the Attunement rule sends the model to <progression> for triggers although they are in <world>, which says reach-salt gives +30 to 40 progress. When the flag is set, the 3-day salt fever ends with 'Describe the new Stage N marks' although no stage changed.
confirmed.scenario: A model that follows <world> sets attunement_progress +35 itself: the engine caps it at +12 and no fever starts. If the flag is set at Stage 0, day 6 tells the narrator to describe 'the new Stage 0 marks (No kin. Ordinary senses.)'.
confirmed.evidence: 'salt_taken' occurs once in the generated prompt. Override reply inc attunement_progress 35 -> progress 12, fever false, note 'capped at +12 per turn'. Flag path, day 6 pending note: 'The fever has broken this morning. Describe the new Stage 0 marks (No kin. Ordinary senses.)'.
confirmed.fix: Add a rule telling the model to set flags.salt_taken_this_turn the turn salt is swallowed and never add the progress itself; make the fever-break note ask for marks only when the stage actually advanced.

votes.reasoning: I captured the real Halloway turn prompt (probe_vv_1.js): "salt_taken" occurs once, as a key in the <state> flags JSON. The <rules> text never mentions flags, and the only related text is the generic "flags.<key>" note on <state>. The Attunement rule (worlds/halloway.js:26) points to <progression> for triggers, but <progression> holds only stages and advanceText. The +30 to 40 reach-salt trigger sits in <world> (halloway.js:39) and the reach-salt lore entry (halloway.js:180), and neither names the flag. index.html:853-855 caps progress at +12, and probe_hw_12.js reproduced progress 12, fever false and the note "attunement_progress capped at +12 per turn". index.html:898 gives no check that the stage advanced, and probe_hw_5.js reproduced the day-6 note "Describe the new Stage 0 marks (No kin. Ordinary senses.)", which contradicts advanceText ("Between advances, nothing visible changes"). Stage 0 is where a salt fever is most likely to happen. The fever-break half is deterministic on the flag path. The first half depends on the model not inferring the flag from its self-descriptive name, so its likelihood is unverified, and that is the only reason to hesitate on severity. Separate observation: the flag path at index.html:887-893 never touches reach_salt_possessed, so salt use only decrements it if the model does so.

confirmed.title: Failed import replaces the live adventure and world before validating, so a malformed save breaks the page and can poison the next boot
confirmed.summary: importFile calls setWorld and assigns adv from the file before checking that state, memory and turns exist; the world check WORLDS[wid] is truthy for inherited names such as constructor. The catch only shows 'Import failed', leaving a half-built unsaved adventure (and possibly another world) current.
confirmed.scenario: A hand-edited, truncated or other-version save without state/memory reports Import failed, but the old adventure is gone from memory; the next turn or render fails with 'Page error while rendering' until reload. A Settings change then persists a doc without state, and the next boot says 'Your saved adventure could not be loaded' because boot tries only the newest doc. A settings.narrTier of bogus imports fine and fails every turn.
confirmed.evidence: probe_p5_4: 'Import failed: ... reading tf', next turn 'Page error ... reading weekday'; probe_p1_9: 'Import failed ... reading facts' then 'Page error ... reading weekday', world title switched; probe_ui_10: Settings change stores a doc with no state key, reboot 'could not load saves: undefined is not valid JSON' (relies on mock dropping undefined fields); probe_sec_3: 8 malformed imports, worldId constructor gives empty #worldTitle; probe_sec_9: store doc with worldId constructor makes boot report 'could not be loaded'.
confirmed.repro: probes/probe_p5_4.js, probe_p1_9.js, probe_ui_10.js, probe_sec_3.js, probe_sec_9.js, probe_rt_5.js (b), probe_ps_8.js (IMP1/IMP2)
confirmed.fix: Build and validate the new adventure into locals (own-property world check, object-typed state and memory, array turns, tier whitelist) and call setWorld and assign adv only after validation succeeds, restoring the previous ones on failure; make boot fall back to the next-newest save and treat a doc without state as unloadable.

votes.reasoning: The core is real. importFile calls setWorld(wid) at index.html:1863 and replaces `adv` at 1864 before `adv.memory.facts` (1866) can throw. Re-running probe_p1_9.js and probe_ui_10.js gave "Import failed ... reading 'facts'", a switched world title, and "Page error while rendering ... reading 'weekday'". probe_ui_10 also stored a state-less doc, and the reboot said "could not be loaded". It is overstated because the trigger is narrow: my probe shows the page's own export always contains state and memory, and no other save format exists ("other-version" is speculation). Nothing stored is lost: persist() is never reached on failure, and in probe_vimp5_1.js, reopening Adventures and pressing Continue restored the original adventure and the next turn ran with no errors. Poisoning the next boot needs a second persisting action (a Settings change) on the broken page, and its dependence on the real runtime dropping `state: undefined` is unverified. Even then the original stays reachable through the Adventures list, since boot's limit(1) (2567) only affects the auto-load. The 'constructor' world-id part is contrived: importing it writes W.id (undefined) via advDoc, so probe_sec_9's seeded store doc is not reachable from the UI. The bogus narrTier case is real (a turn gives "invalid_request — unknown modelTier bogus"; the Settings select shows blank), but it needs a hand-crafted file and is fixed by picking a tier. A related minor defect I also saw: after a failed import the Adventures dialog stays open with a stale list, and the original row says "Current", so clicking it only closes the dialog.

The catch maps it to 'Page error: ...' at 1604, with no retry. I found no guard or alternative path that makes this unreachable, and state is rolled back at 1608, so there is no corruption and low severity fits. confirmed.title: Override 'Apply as turn' leaves the 'folding memory…' status banner up indefinitely
confirmed.summary: commitReply sets the status to 'folding memory…' when sample is connected, but applyManualReply never clears it as takeTurn does.

The finding's "14-turn adventure" detail is incidental: the status is set unconditionally before foldBeats, so it sticks on any turn. refuted.title: Glutton guardian 'does not let go' conflicts with the rule that the player can always leave
refuted.why: The two phrases are real: rule 18 (worlds/sundered.js:34) says "{first} can always leave", and the Glutton entry (sundered.js:766) says "it embraces, and does not let go, and can be talked to". The same sentence supplies the reconciliation, because "can be talked to" is the sanctioned way the embrace ends. The finding's second branch ("a release that breaks the guardian's description") is therefore false: releasing {first} once they ask, or are talked round, is exactly what the description allows. The text reaches the narrator as flavour inside the GM block (index.html:1255, "Guardian: ..."), alongside the explicit general rule at line 34. The Hoard, Siren and Sleeper entries use similarly absolute language, and none of them forces a contradiction. I found no code, guard or observed run showing a forced choice, and the narrator's behaviour could not be tested because the harness has no real model, so this is a stylistic wording tension rather than a defect. I noticed no new distinct defect.
